utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Court Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we hear the testimony of the next witness, I'd like to briefly address the issue of expert reports. On the 5th of June, the Chamber instructed the Defence to file monthly updates on the progress of expert reports. The first report was sent by e-mail rather than filed on the record. The following report was filed after the dead-line. Furthermore, all of the reports were incomplete and despite numerous reminders the Defence has not rectified these incompletenesses. Mr. Lukic, do you have any explanation for the failure to comply with the Chamber's instructions so that we can consider any further steps?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I know, Your Honours, is that we have a problem with contacting some of our expert witnesses. One of them was injured and in the hospital with a broken arm, I think. And the other one has not finished his work yet, that's a mining expert. I know about that. I know that we have a problem with submitting those expertises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, isn't the purpose of regular reports that the Chamber becomes aware of this rather than have to inquire after it all happened so that you inform us about when this person broke his arm and what are the consequences, and why one of them has not finished his work so that we could see what could best be done under those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The -- the second one would -- didn't -- have not -- has not finished his work yet. I had to obtain some documents from land registrars from various cities where the mosques were, churches were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, that's exactly what reporting is good for. That if he would need the assistance of the Chamber in order to get them, that we would be able to provide that assistance. We also could inquire into when he asked it for the first time, whether it's the expert who failed to do what he had to do or that he only asked for it yesterday and now says, "I don't have the reports." I mean, that's exactly the purpose of reporting, that we can -- that we are better able to see what should be done. But let's leave it to that at this moment. There are at least three things that need to be done at this very moment. First of all, the latest update report, which was during the 20th of August, has not been received. Can you tell us when you filed it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to check if it's filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you -- yes, of course, if it has been filed meanwhile, then most likely we would know about it. But if it has been done in the last half an hour, we might have missed it. So would you please inform us today when it will be filed. Then on the 16th of July, and please have a look at transcript page 24173, the Chamber instructed the Defence to file its prior two updates which were sent by e-mails of the 3rd and the 20th of June. And could you tell us when they will be filed? Because, as you may remember, it was -- filing was the instruction, not just sending e-mails.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably we were mislead by the practice that a lot of things are done through e-mails. So I don't think that we planned to file it, but if you order it so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we did so. We did so on the 16th of July. But could I expect that if you have verified the reference page, that you would file them within the next 24 hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To be on the safe side, can we get 48 hours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You get 48 hours. Then the last issue is that three proposed expert witnesses have never been addressed in the Defence's report. These are Keserovic, Krcmar, and Stankovic. When will the Defence file an update on these witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll file it, then, with the update we have to file on the -- everybody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So that is within the next 48 hours. Okay. Then we are about ready to hear the testimony of the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are, Your Honour. It should be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could -- could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the time to deal with the following. On the 15th of July, the Prosecution informed the Chamber via an informal communication of its progress on several issues related to maps which had been used during the testimony of Witness Milos Skrba. The Chamber was informed that the parties agreed, tentatively, on some of the issues. Regarding the remaining issues, however, the Prosecution stated that it expects the Defence to take action. This was reiterated via an informal commutation on the 30th of July 2014. The Chamber would like to inquire whether there has been any progress on the matter, and we, of course, since it was announced that the Defence would take an initiative, what we could expect from the Defence at this moment? If you would like to respond later today, that's fine, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to inquire first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I had forgotten that it was announced that the OTP would have a brief preliminary matter to raise.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, about 50 words. I would advise the Trial Chamber that with respect to yesterday's discussion at transcript 24672 to lines 20 through 22, we reviewed the trial record for the instances cited by the Defence counsel. We believe that the trial record is both accurate and speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: As a result, we will not be filing additional submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Ms. Bibles. For us to understand, does this support or not support the Defence's position?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We do not believe it support it is Defence's position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And you say that will be clear from the sources. Good morning, Witness, Mr. Adzic, I assume. Mr. Adzic, before you give evidence in this court, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Adzic. Please be seated. Mr. Adzic, you will first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You'll find him to your left. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Adzic.

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First, can we have a look at 1D1634.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the meantime, I could remind you, Mr. Lukic, you should ask the witness for his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we go on, Mr. Adzic, please tell us for the record what your first and last name is. It is just for the purposes of the record.

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Ratko Adzic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic is kindly asked to wait for the B/C/S translation to be finished before he begins speaking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters, Mr. Lukic, are kindly asking you to wait for the B/C/S translation to be finished before to resume speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will go to English channel so I don't make any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the screen before you --

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- you see a signature. Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: I don't see any signatures on the screen. I only see printed text. Oh, yes, on the right-hand side. I apologise. You mean the witness statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: It is my signature. I apologise. I was looking at the left-hand side screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you indeed provide a statement to representatives of General Mladic's Defence?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go to the last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see a signature here and do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The statement you provided to General Mladic's Defence, is it accurate and truthful?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you were asked the same questions today, would you, in principle, answer the same way?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would like to have this statement into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D01634 receives number D597, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the absence of any objections, D597 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read a short summary of the statement of this witness, and then I will just have a few questions for him. May I, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness Adzic Ratko was born on 5/11/1948 in the village of Kadarici, Ilijas municipality, Sarajevo. He currently resides in Belgrade, Republic of Serbia. In relevant period he was the president of municipality of Ilijas, as of 1st January 1991. After that he became the president of Crisis Staff in Ilijas municipality, and at the same time he continued to be the president of municipality. From 20th of January 1993 until July 1993, he was the minister of internal affairs in Republika Srpska. The witness will testify on overall situation in BiH before and after the first multi-party elections in 1990, and functioning of municipality authorities. He will testify on the census of population conducted in 1991, and on the demographic situation in Ilijas municipality where he was the president of the same. He will testify on functioning and work of municipality authorities, creation and activities of national parties such as HDZ and SDA, and activities of their representatives in the municipality of Ilijas. The witness will testify on creation of Crisis Staff staff in the Ilijas municipality, its structure, composition, and activity of its members, implementation of its decisions, as well as of the relationship of the civilian and the military authorities. Also, this witness has knowledge on organisation and the armament of Muslim and Croat population, on creation of paramilitary units as Green Berets and Patriotic League, their training and activities, particularly in emerge of conflict in former Yugoslavia. He will testify on his work during his tenure as minister of the interior in Republika Srpska and will explain his knowledge on relationship between police and VRS in the relevant period. He will explain structure and functioning of the MUP and command and control over police units, and modalities of their engagement in operations in the relevant period. That would be a short summary, and I will just have a few questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put them to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adzic, was a Crisis Staff formed in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It was established in late December 1991 on recommendation from the presidency of Republika Srpska and its national assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While the Crisis Staff was in operation, was the municipal assembly in operation as well?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: It was. Let me clarify. Given the fact that the assembly bodies, the executive council, and other administrative bodies functioned, there was no need for the Crisis Staff to take their place, but it was set up because the situation was becoming more serious and the war was looming. It was actually established in order to provide defence and protect the resources of the RS so that people would be designated who were supposed to be held accountable for preserving those and to secure their proper functioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How were the members of the staff appointed?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: On recommendation, the municipal president was the president of the Crisis Staff. As for the secretary and other staff, the Serb representatives, that is, in the municipality itself, also were made members of the Crisis Staff. It also included the head of the police station and managers of some state-owned enterprises which covered the issues of supplies, commodity reserves, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were any members of the Crisis Staff also members of the JNA or later VRS?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: No. If I may, I'd like to clarify. Before that, the civilian protection of the Serbian people staff was established on recommendation from the SDS, and the territorial units were established which then became units of the VRS. Members of that staff had the exclusively obligation to organise the Serbian people for defence. Their domain regarded the issue I mentioned, and there was no need for them to be engaged as members of the Crisis Staff as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to change topics now and ask you whether in Ilijas after the outbreak of the conflict, the Muslim population remained, left, separated, or whatever? Please explain the ethnic structure of the municipality following the outbreak of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: If I may, I'd like to invoke the 1991 census in Bosnia-Herzegovina. As regards the municipality of Ilijas, it had around 25.000 inhabitants. Ten and a half thousand of them were Muslims, 11.600 Serbs, 1.700 Croats, and some 2.000 pronounced themselves as Yugoslavs and the rest. So in total, around 25.000. The ethnic structure? Well, Ilijas is a small town and with its urban nucleus. The rest of the municipality covered villages and hamlets. The villages were either Serbian or Muslim or Croatian. We agreed with the representatives of the Muslim people, the SDA, and the HDZ, that the bodies they were to form in the territory inhabited by Croats or Muslims, they were to take up responsibility in organising the system of functioning for the authorities. Just before the outbreak of the war, in March 1992, there was a division in the police station. On my initiative, I called a general meeting including representatives of the SDA and HDZ and proposed that all of the policemen, who -- of whom ten or eleven were Muslim, would receive all weapons and equipment so that they can establish, in agreement with the political representatives of the SDA, the functioning of their police in the territory inhabited by Muslims. Prior to that, the HDZ and the SDA, when the assembly was divided in 1992, established their own municipal body. I apologise, that was in 1991, December 1991. They had their own bodies of authority and they were responsible for their work. In all parts of the municipality inhabited by Muslims or Croats, the functioning of authorities was organised by the SDA and HDZ. They had their own police station, and all of the policemen - who were Muslim or Croatian - worked in that station and were responsible to their own bodies. We did the same in the territories inhabited by Serbs, that included the police station of Ilijas which was responsible for law and order. It was agreed that the Serb police was not to enter Muslim settlements without previous announcement, and if there were any incidents they were to be tackled jointly. So each side covered their own ethnic territory, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long was that agreement in place?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Until the 3rd of May, 1992, when the first bigger offensive took place launched by Muslims from Visoko and Breza. On the 3rd of May at around 10.00 a.m., there was intensive shelling of Ilijas and the settlements around it such as Podlugovi and the attack on defence lines in Cekrcici and other villages. There was fighting all day long. We repelled the attack, defended our territory, and later on there was no longer any communication with the Muslim authorities save for a few instances when I was invited to attend. It was actually before the 26th of April that I attended a meeting in Visoko, the municipal president of Visoko and Breza was there and we tried to establish some kind of co-operation. I was always open for any agreement, anything that would protect the interests of all peoples, and I was there to represent the interests of the Serbian people. But I also accepted that the Muslims and Croats also had to protect their own interests. After the 3rd of May when the attack occurred -- I apologise. There was another round of talks on the 3rd of May organised by the municipal president of Breza, Mr. Opacina [phoen], sometime in the afternoon. I went to Breza, together with the brigade commander, Markovo Polje [phoen]. We analysed the reasons for the attack. I asked them why they attacked us, and I located their precise artillery position which they used to shell the centre of Ilijas. The very first shell that came from Breza killed a Muslim, interestingly enough. He was seriously wounded at the time. In Ilijas, we had no hospital resources and could not treat seriously wounded. There was an ambulance which took him to the Kosevo hospital in Sarajevo together with his wife. Upon his return at Kobilja Glava, the Green Berets, having realised that the ambulance was driven by a Serb driver wanted to kill him and take the vehicle. But the wife of the wounded Muslim saved him. She explained that she had no means to return to Ilijas, started to cry, and they released the ambulance. After that I called an SDA representative, and I said that I could not longer send Serb drivers to take the wounded Muslims to Muslim controlled areas, otherwise I would be endangering their lives. We agreed that if a Muslim were wounded, they were to organise transport and we would provide gas. And then they took their wounded either to Visoko -- well, mostly to Visoko because it was the easiest thing to do. It went on until the 3rd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did the war in Bosnia start, according to you?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: On the 4th of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So from the 4th of April until the 3rd of May, the agreement on co-operation --

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: That agreement was in place and it was honoured by both sides, by Muslims and by my side, of course, as the representative of the Serbian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And all the party agreement on the transport of the wounded, when was that made?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Somewhat earlier -- actually, it was on the 3rd of May. On the 3rd of May, because a girl was wounded in Bircana [phoen] during shelling. She was a Muslim, and her father brought her in a car. But she was so seriously wounded that she couldn't be hospitalised there and that's why they suggested that she should be transported to Visoko. No ambulance was needed but we provided them with fuel, and some relatives of hers transported her to Visoko and they returned. Then I talked to the President of the SDA, Mehed Mesovic [phoen], and we agreed that all the cases of the wounded Muslims, because they did not have resources to care for the Muslims, that all the Muslim civilians in the city would be transported to Visoko and we would supply them with fuel for that transportation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Obviously they could choose to be treated at Serbian hospitals, in Pale, for example, but they wanted to go to Visoko. That was their choice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters ask you to slow down so that they are able to translate all your words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Teachers are known to speak faster more than lawyers.

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it goes then with the job.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When it comes to Ilijas -- or, rather, all of the parts of Ilijas municipality, were they all under Serb control?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: No, no. All parts of Ilijas municipality and the villages, they were mixed - the Muslim and Serb villages. That's how things were. We talked to the representatives of the Muslim powers, and we agreed that in all of the villages where the Muslim population prevailed they should organise their authorities. Neither I nor the Serbian bodies had any control of that territory. We knew that the units of the Patriotic League were being armed. As we spoke to the representatives of the SDA, we confronted them with that fact. We told them that we are aware of that, that we considered that to be their choice, and that we would not undertake any measures in order to prevent them from doing that because that was their choice. However, we also told them that we should agree that everybody should protect their own village and their own settlement, and us Serbs, we did that as well. That agreement was honoured and no armed formations crossed over from one village to the other. Only our chosen representatives could talk to each other and deal with some issues at hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Serbs leave Ilijas?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did. If you will allow me just briefly. The situation was created after the 4th of April. The war had started. That was obvious. I talked to the police and the Red Cross. During that period of time, there was a wave of displaced persons coming from Central Bosnia, Visoko, Konjic, and Breza. The situation was very chaotic. A lot of people needed assistance. They needed food and medical aid, and we hardly had resources for that. When it comes to the movement of people, I ordered the enforcement bodies not to prevent people from moving around, not to restrict that freedom. When it comes to the town itself and its centre, we had a lot of ethnic groups there, but in that period of time they could talk to the Red Cross. They could give them the statement in order to cross the check-points that were controlled by the police on the borders of the municipality. They had the right to leave, nobody could bother them. Some Muslims and Croats left the municipality in that way but also a lot of Serbs did that. I'm again speaking too fast, aren't I? Well, I apologise. During that period, I tried to make sure that everybody had the right of movement, irrespective of their ethnicity. They had the right to choose the place where they wanted to go in light of the dramatic situation that prevailed in the area at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My next question is this -- or, rather, I already asked you whether Muslims and Croats were leaving and you already answered. However, when we are talking about the departure of Muslims and Croats and you said that they did leave, was there a plan in place for the expulsion of Muslims and Croats from Ilijas municipality?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not. No. It was their own free movement, their free departure, which was the result of the chaotic situation. It was their personal choice to leave the war-struck area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there any people who decided to leave but then returned?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of just one case. But that happened in the month of June. There was an accident resulting from a conflict between Muslims and Croats in Ilijas. There was an exchange of the population in agreement with the Muslim authorities in Breza and Visoko. All of that was organised with the help of the Red Cross. It was broadcast in the media that everybody who wanted to leave Ilijas or Breza could do that freely. They could go to Visoko. The Serbs wanted to come from Breza and Visoko to Ilijas and Muslims wanted to go to Breza. There was one case, as far as I know, that a Muslim who applied, together with his son, I believe that his name was Mujo Dzafic, he was put on the exchange list, he headed for Breza. And later he told me about the incident that had occurred and he returned to Ilijas. I didn't know it on the day the Red Cross was involved in that. On the following day, he wanted me to see him as the president of the municipality. I received him to see what the situation was all about, and he asked me, "President, can I stay in Ilijas?" And I said, "Why not? Every citizen has a choice. But you have to be aware that you will have to share the situation as it is with the rest of us. Whatever we have you will have and every other citizen, of course." And then he said, "I want to stay." And then he was -- since he was an acquaintance of a military police unit, he told me he wanted to join that unit because he trusted his acquaintance. And I said this does not depend on me, it depends on the secretariat of defence in the municipality and the brigade command. Obviously whoever wanted to volunteer and join any of the units, he would not be denied that opportunity and that's how he actually joined that unit, and this is the only case that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I again ask you to slow down because part of your testimony will be lost if you continue in this speed of speech.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best to slow down. I'll try and focus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After the conflicts started, can you just briefly tell us whether there was an exit from Ilijas towards the Serb held territory? How wide was that corridor? Which other municipalities were forced to use that corridor? Were you encircled? Were you in a semi-encirclement? Just briefly answer.

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: In very brief outlines, let me you. Ilijas was blockaded to -- in the direction of Visoko, Breza, and Olovo, and we could not use any roads in those directions. Across Vogosca municipality towards Sarajevo, all the roads were blocked. So we could leave Ilijas only via Semizovac towards Srednje. And there was a mountain road there which had been used for forestry purposes. Wood was transported across Visojevica. We repaired that road, and that was the only road. But even that was not safe. There were Muslim villages on both sides, and there were frequent attacks. Fire was often opened for the columns of vehicle that used that road. That was our only communication with Pale, and that communication was used by Vogosca, Rajlovac, Hadzici, and Ilijici. That was the only exit and only road leading to Pale at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that, as a matter of fact, the entire road was within the outer ring of the BiH Army forces?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Or, no. Or rather, partly from Semizovac to Srednje, it was not safe. On the left-hand side there were Croat-Muslim villages, Ostomorine and Korota [phoen]. There were no military units there due to the configuration of the terrain, so the road could not be protected. That's why we used military escorts for buses and vehicles like that. The police and the military secured us such convoys until they reached Srednje from where they were safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd like to tackle another topic, and we will finish with that. Please tell us briefly whether there were any attempts to hand over absolute property rights or either the sale of property and cars. How was that dealt with in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: On the 4th of April, when we realised that the situation was very dramatic and that the war had started, people were obviously scared. They were afraid. I was aware of the situation, but my first warning of the possible abuse of the situation -- or, rather, it was the chief of the secretary for administration who warned me about that. A Serb, possibly with a criminal record, arrived at the secretariat for administration and requested for a sale contract for a house to be stamped. He -- the person who sold the house was a Croat. I inquired about the situation, then -- then I realised this -- there was room for possible abuse. I made the decision, which I conveyed to all the municipality organs, according to which during that period the bodies of the municipal assembly in charge of property matters were not allowed to register any sales or purchase agreement or transfer a property deed, and that included apartments, houses, and cars. Thus I prevented possible manipulations and abuses, because there were identified criminals who were capable of making the most of the fear of individuals later on. And it turned out that some of them had three or four, or even five purchase agreements according to which they allegedly bought apartments from their original owners. But those were not registered and those contracts were never made valid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Only now the interpretation was finished. You should really slow down. It's impossible for the interpreters to follow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a teacher. It's a habit, and old habits die hard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But even teachers should learn something.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't agree more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Adzic, this is all that we had to ask you, and I would like to thank you for answering our questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Fluegge has a question before the Prosecution will start its cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to explain one matter of timing, which I really didn't understand. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm listening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said, and this is on page 12: "After the 3rd of May when the attack occurs," and then some lines down at the beginning of page 13, you said: "The very first shell that came from Breza killed a Muslim." Then you explain how you reached an agreement with the Croatian --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 3rd of May, yes. The 3rd of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The 3rd of May, indeed. And then you explain how you reach an agreement with the other side about transportation of wounded people. And then you said, this is page 13, line 19: "It went on until the 3rd of May 1992," this agreement. Perhaps it was a slip of the tongue. Explain the dates again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I meant the 3rd of June. When it comes to the transportation of wounded people, the agreement was in place until the 3rd of June. Why the 3rd of June? Because on the 3rd of June, there was a second offensive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I just wanted to ask you a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- clarification of the date. Now you say it went on until the 3rd of June, 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The agreement on the transportation of wounded people. That was in place until the 3rd of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said the 3rd of May, I probably had a different development or event in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it was a slip of the tongue. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one or two questions for you as well. In your statement, we do not find a lot about the establishment of the Crisis Staff. Neither about your position as president of the Crisis Staff. You said it was established in December 1991. Was this openly done or was it secretly done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was done openly. The municipal assembly of Ilijas functioned and it had all of its bodies. Perhaps it was not even necessary to set up a Crisis Staff. However, we honoured the decision of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me first -- I didn't ask you whether it was necessary or not but just on whether it was openly done or secretly done. You've answered that question. You also said that it was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precise -- yes, it was done openly. It was done publicly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you said it was done, and that's where I interrupted you, on the instructions of whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a recommendation by the presidency of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The presidency, the complete presidency --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A complete presidency. Yes, the complete presidency of Republika Srpska. That's what we saw in their letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. They sent a letter to whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Personally, I think it was sent to all the presidents of the municipalities where they existed or those Serb bodies who -- which had been set up in the Serbian territory before the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said, "... sent to all the presidents of the municipalities where they existed," what do you mean by "they"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the elections, there was a distribution of power in all of the 109 municipalities. Where the SDS participated in the elections, it had the right to participate in the authorities of that municipality, its representatives. There were places where they were a minority, there were places where they did not even exist, and there were places where they were a majority. And based on the relationship of the participation of powers in every municipality, if there was a nucleus of Serbian representatives in that power, they inherited that line of management as bodies of the Serbian political authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was this a public decision where it was represented to establish the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. The Assembly of Republika Srpska was already set up after the division in the parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The government of Republika Srpska was also established, and the establishment of all the other bodies including ministries was underway. There was also a presidency which comprised the president, the vice-president, and so on and so forth. Those were legitimate decisions made by the state bodies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't ask you whether it was legitimate or not. I only asked you whether it was public or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, then. Yes, of course. It was public. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, finally, do I understand that you were, as the -- and I'm reading from paragraph 18 of your statement, that as the president of the Crisis Staff, that Serb units, until the establishment of the Army of Republika Srpska, were under your command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partly, yes. Partly. Those were TO units of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you say "partly." Was there any other Serb units not commanded by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there were in other units. There were only TO units. And the reason why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. What does then "partly" mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said partly, meaning that the brigade commander was appointed when the staff was established. We tried to select trained officers. Obviously they were responsible, and they were in charge of decision-making. However, that was a TO unit. We consulted each other. If their decisions went beyond the scope of defence, those decisions obviously concerned the use of those units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Ms. Bibles, I'm looking at the clock, perhaps it would be better to start the cross-examination after the break, and take an early break. We take a break, Mr. Adzic, of 20 minutes. We would like to see you back. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to be brought in, I briefly deal with the following matter. It's about P6680 and P6682. During the testimony of Milutin Vujicic on the 17th of July, the Prosecution indicated that the parties would discuss a possible agreement on whether certain portions of P6680 and P6682 should be tendered. On the 25th of August, the Prosecution informed the Chamber through an informal communication that no agreement was reached with regard to P6682 and that the Defence intended to make written submissions. With regard to P6680, the Prosecution indicated that the parties agreed to tender the entire document but that there were some translation issues for which the Prosecution had already made the appropriate requests. The Chamber notes that the document is 74 pages long, and the Chamber is not inclined to admit it in its entirety. The Chamber, therefore, gives the parties one week to file submissions explaining why they deem it necessary to admit the document in its entirety rather than the portions that were discussed with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Adzic, you'll now be cross-examined by Ms. Bibles. Ms. Bibles speaks slowly. You're invited to do the same. You'll find Ms. Bibles to your right. Ms. Bibles is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Adzic, in your statement and in your testimony, you describe being elected to the local SDS board. Isn't it true that you were also elected a member to the SDS Main Board starting in 1991?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: It is correct. I practically participated in the establishment of the SDS. I was elected a member of the SDS Main Board, and I was one of the main organisers of the SDS in the territory of the Ilijas municipality. Based on that, I was elected president of the SDS council that was registered in August 1991 with the competent authorities of BiH as a legitimate political party preparing itself for the elections.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I want to turn now to your discussion about paragraph 18 of your statement and some of the questions right before we went to break. This has to do with the Serb units that made up the defence of Ilijas prior to the formation of the VRS. You've told us that the TO was -- made up part of these units. Were the Serbian police also part of these units?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: The Serbian police did not make part of those units until the 30th of March 1992 when there was a split in the police at the republican level. On the 30th of March, the Ilijas police station also reflected that division. It was divided into the Serbian and Muslim police station. In agreement with the SDA and HDZ on my proposal, since in some other police stations some Serbians were arrested or persecuted, I insisted that the Muslim members of the police be allowed to take material and equipment assigned to each policeman so that they could establish their own police station in the territory where they believed necessary in order to set up police authority in the settlements where there was a majority Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can we agree that the VRS was formed on the 12th of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: I think the Main Staff, by a decision of the RS presidency, was formed on the 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it accurate that the Ilijas Light Infantry Brigade was created on the 27th of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Don't hold me exactly to the date given the number of years that have passed, but it was around that time. It was pursuant to the -- to a decision of the Serbian Crisis Staff headed by Mr. Bogdan Jevtic, a colonel. It was on his proposal that the established TO units were placed under a single command and the unit called the Ilijas Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it true that this initial brigade was comprised of ten infantry companies and a mixed artillery division?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: At the moment of establishment, we did not have a mixed artillery regiment. It was only established later. The TO companies that existed at the time -- well, I don't know whether there was -- there were precisely 14, but the number of TO companies that existed before that was the number of the companies that made part of the Ilijas Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Perhaps we should take a look at the order establishing the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have P3797 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that to come up. Mr. Adzic, I asked you before the break - clearly - whether there were any other units than the TO that were referred to in paragraph 18 and were under the command of the Crisis Staff. You said there were no other units, whereas I now understand from your previous answer that from the 30th of March - that is the whole month of April - and the beginning of May that, that the police forces were among those units as well. Where I specifically asked you whether there were any other units, you said there were not. It now turns out that police units were, at least during five or six weeks, part of that. Will you please, instead of giving long answers not always related to the questions, would you focus on what is asked and would you please be precise in your answers. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is. Perhaps I misunderstood, especially in terms of time, because the police separated only as late as the 30th of March. That is why I didn't pay attention to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked you about the time until the establishment of the VRS, which was on the 12th of May. So perhaps you should be focused more listening to the question rather than expanding on matters which are not asked. Ms. Bibles, if the witness goes, dwells away from what you ask him, please stop him and bring him back to what you asked him. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 2 in the English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- we're looking at the 27th May 1992 description of the creation of the Ilijas Light Infantry Brigade. And I'd ask you to look in section 2. It's the second bullet pointed area where it's describing the brigade. Excuse me, I'm sorry. In the first bullet point, where it indicates: "There are ten infantry companies and a mixed artillery division in the brigade." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, ten. I can see. It is on the 27th. I apologise. The report is dated the 27th of May. In the meantime, the brigade --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness trailed off. Could he kindly repeat the end of his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could -- oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could you tell us the end of your last answer? We were not able to articulate it.

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: When the corps command was established around the 20th of May, any further structuring and organisation as well as arming fell within the competence of the corps command. Before the 20th of May, as part of the brigade, there was no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- specific location where the MAP was designated, the mixed artillery battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you're not here to give any lessons. You're here to answer a question. The only question that was put to you was whether you saw, in this document, what Ms. Bibles referred to. Wait for --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- any further question. And Ms. Bibles will be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- precise on it. Ms. Bibles, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you had a position of authority with respect to the Ilijas Light Infantry Brigade in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Not in the sense of a particular position in the brigade. I was simply the municipal president and the president of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In your capacity as president -- municipal president and president of the Crisis Staff, did you have any type of authority over the light brigade?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: I did have authority in consulting the command in certain circumstances if they so required.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to 65 ter 3714.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, this is a letter, it appears, that you wrote to President Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, before we go into some of the areas that are raised in this letter, this may be an appropriate time for the witness to receive a caution regarding 90(E).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Ms. Bibles asked me to give a caution under Rule 90(E). You may not be aware of what that is, but I'll explain it to you. If any of the answers you would give to any of the questions put by Ms. Bibles, if any of those answers might tend to incriminate yourself, then you may object to answer such a question. The Chamber will then consider whether or not we'll compel you to answer the question. Now, if we do compel you to answer the question, your answer shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against yourself for any offence other than false testimony. So if you are afraid that you would -- that the answer would tend to incriminate yourself, you may address me. Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, can you look at the letter on the screen and tell us whether that is your signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We note that it is signed, "Commander of the Ilijas ..." Sorry, "the army of the Serbian people in Bosnian and Herzegovina." Can you explain to us what that position means?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention to it. It was probably it the typist's habit. In practice, that was the way the Crisis Staff command was designated. He probably typed it that way because it was considered to be the command of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, this is a letter that you've told us that you're writing to the president of the Republika Srpska. Are we to understand that you didn't look at the title under which you were writing that letter before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: It doesn't say "VRS."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could you read what the title says?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: It could be treated as "The Military Forces of the Territorial Defence." I coordinated those forces at the time and that is what the abbreviation stand for.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, does it not read: "Commander of the Ilijas VSN BiH"?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, of the municipality of Ilijas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, VSN stands for what, literally? Not your explanation, but what does VSN stand for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was considered to be the military forces of the Territorial Defence. It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- had been established at the time, but it was in the stage of harmonisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not teaching. I asked you VSN, three letters, stand for what, exactly? I expect three words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The military forces of Ilijas. And it was understood to mean the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Witness, again, I instructed you not to give your explanation at this moment but just to give us the three words. You apparently ignore my instructions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And no loud speaking from Mr. Mladic. No speaking aloud.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The VS stands for military forces. As for the N, it is "peoples." That is what was understood. That is why you do not find the acronym TO. I was the municipal president representing the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- inhabitants of the Serbian municipality of Ilijas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now instruct you clearly to answer questions. And if I said twice to you that I'm not seeking your explanation but that I'm just asking you a very specific question, if you continue like this, we may have to take measures which possibly could include that your testimony will be invalid before this Court. That is a possible consequence if you continue to act like you do at this moment. Ms. Bibles, I would appreciate if you would also pay attention to the heading of this letter. I don't know whether you intended to do that, but especially the third line.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, in trying to articulate what this letter means both in terms of your position and what is going on at the time, I'll ask you to please read the very top three lines of this letter.

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: "It is my pleasure to inform you" --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, sir --

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: -- "that in the battles waged thus far" --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: At the very top of the letter, the very left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: At the very beginning?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, the very beginning, which indicates --

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. Okay. Yes. [Interpretation] Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Serbian municipality of Ilijas. Command of the Ilijas Serbian army. To the president of the presidency of the Serbian Republic of BiH. "It is my pleasure to inform you that" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "... that in the battles waged thus far, the enemy forces ..." Is that what you want?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sir, you were asked to read the first three lines. Please try to carefully listen to the question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, in looking at the first three lines on the upper left-hand side, doesn't this suggest - in fact, openly state - that you were writing President Karadzic as the commander of the Serbian -- of the Ilijas Serbian army command?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: President Karadzic, as RS president, was the Supreme Commander. We followed that line of authority and we addressed him on behalf of the military units command. It was considered appropriate for me to address the president of the republic in that way. That is what it means.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, let's turn now to the content of the letter. Without reading it verbatim, is it accurate to say that you were asking President Karadzic to use his influence to obtain very specific military equipment for the Ilijas Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: That is correct. Precisely because --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That's all I asked. We see in the second paragraph that you justify this request by saying: "I need these artillery pieces for further defence and the self-propelled anti-aircraft guns to cleanse certain pieces of terrain in the Ilijas municipality." Can you tell us in what direction you wanted the self-propelled Praga anti-aircraft guns to be aimed?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: In that period, since the territory of Ilijas municipality is mostly in hilly terrain, there were some sabotage groups, Muslim groups, in parts of our territory which cut off our roads and communication. The army and the command of the Ilijas Brigade could not successfully engage them without additional assets. I had such forested areas in mind. To neutralise those groups which made incursions around the clock in order to secure our communication with Pale, road wise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if I way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Obviously, Ms. Bibles, I don't have English version -- translation, actually, of this document, but "Praga" is not self-propelled. It's a machine-gun. So if it says in the translation "self-propelled" it's not correct. I don't have translation in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You see the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It just says "Praga."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It just says "Praga."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is no "self-propelled." Three Pragas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There may be a translation issue there. So let's forget about the "self-propelled" and let's leave it to "Praga."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, does the fact that you're asking President Karadzic to use his influence to get these weapons for you mean that the SRK command rejected a request to give the brigade this equipment? Do you have an answer?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: This doesn't mean that the request was turned down. Due to the difficult situation and the necessity to equip the units of the brigade as quickly as possible, I tried to ask President Karadzic to speed that process along. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did you reach out to other political leaders at the republic level?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I move to tender 65 ter, I think it's, 3714.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 3714 receives number P6695, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6695 is admitted -- no, is marked for identification pending a verification of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, your letter to President Karadzic was dated 12 June 1992. I'd like to show you an entry from General Mladic's notebook from the following day, which would be 13 June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have P353, page 155 in English and 154 in the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, sir, as this comes up or as it's come up in the original, this entry notes that on this date General Mladic is at a meeting at the presidency. Here in this initial section of that meeting, Mladic reports or refers to "president of Ilijas SO" wants tanks and anti-aircraft weapons. First, can we agree that Mladic is referring to you in this line?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: I assume so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And just for the record, does SO refer to "Srpska Obstina"?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, sir, isn't it true that Ilijas did not get tanks and Praga anti-aircraft weapons from the VRS as a result of your request, did they?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. It received weapons later, but I was not involved in that. It was the corps command who decided on those matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So just to make sure that we understand. In some capacity, military capacity, you wrote to President Karadzic, and the military did -- basically, the military made the decision at the corps level as to what the brigade needed. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: During mid-June --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And we can take this from the screen at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: During mid-June, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, apparently a similar issue arises as Pragas being more or less interpreted as self-propelled anti-aircraft guns. Now, I'm not insisting on a review of the whole of the -- of the notebook, but at least could you try to seek an agreement whether Pragas are in any way self-propelled or whether we should ignore the self-propelling feature of what is called Pragas.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: During mid-1992 at the same time -- excuse me, mid-June, the same time in which you were asking for tanks, isn't it true that you also sent out requests for additional manpower?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: No, I did not send any requests for additional manpower to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 3301 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, when this comes on our screen, we'll see a letter requesting help from the Serb Volunteer Guard for the Ilijas Brigade or the Ilijas municipality. Sir, I'll give a few minutes to review the letter. It appears that you've had a chance to look at it. Did you authorise this request?

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: I can only say that I've not seen this request before. It was not drafted on my request. It doesn't contain a stamp or a signature. I was not familiar with its contents and anybody could have drafted this.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could move to 65 ter 3717 next.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, this appears to be another request for help. This time from the Serbian National Renewal Belgrade. This is dated also 14 -- actually, this one appears -- we believe that there is a, perhaps, a date issue. In any event, please take a look at this letter and tell us whether you authorise this request.

utterances.speaker: RATKO ADZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, then --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could turn to 65 ter 10722.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you do that, then I would like to ask the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did anybody tell you about this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not about the document. However, at the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I -- I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I heard from a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- I'm asking about the document. I'm only asking about this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Have you any explanation about why your name is written at the end of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Anybody's name can appear in any document. I didn't know anything about this document. I tried to explain, with your leave, of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I don't -- you said you don't have any explanation for that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I'd -- at this time if we could go to 65 ter 10722.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, this appears to be a similar, although longer letter. Now, sir, the three requests have all born very similar information on the upper left-hand corner as to where they were coming from, including numbers. Can you tell us whether the numbering at the upper left-hand corner --

utterances.speaker: Can you tell us if you ever seen this document which is now on
utterances.text: [In English] No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- is something that looks familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: Can you tell us if you ever seen this document which is now on
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Usually documents contain protocol numbers and it seems that somebody used random numbers. I have never seen these documents before. And, as you can see for yourself, I never signed them. At that time, anybody could draft a document of this kind. I claim categorically I had absolutely nothing to do with these documents. I don't know about them. They were not drafted on my instruction. I didn't draft them myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree that there were already Serb volunteers in Ilijas by June of 1992 as part of the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: Can you tell us if you ever seen this document which is now on
utterances.text: Organised volunteer forces did not exist. There was not a single unit. All the units that were armed were part of the Ilijas Brigade. There were perhaps individual cases or, rather, individuals who arrived from other territories in Ilijas and they joined voluntarily because they couldn't be mobilised. That's why they were considered volunteers in the units of the Ilijas Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could go to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we go -- again, carefully look at the question. The question was whether there were already Serb volunteers in Ilijas by June of 1992 as part of the Serb forces. You started your answer by saying "Organised volunteer forces did not exist ..." The real answer is that volunteers may have been in the Serb forces in Ilijas by June of 1992. No one asked you whether they were organised as volunteer units. The question was whether volunteers were there and apparently the answer is yes, that, at least, on an individual basis. Please start your answer to focus on the question rather than to what apparently you consider more important to tell us. Most important is an answer to the question. Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we go to the end of the document in both languages. I am not sure if we are at -- really at the bottom of the page in B/C/S. I would like to see the far end. Witness, do you see in the B/C/S at the end there is a kind of an initial or minimal handwriting thing. Do you know what that could mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Which initials do you have in mind? I can't find them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't know if that -- if these are initials --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you mean the initial which looks like a cross, like an encircled cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Possible. At the end of the document, I assume that you see the words "president of the Crisis Staff." There is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and then it says "SSR," I don't know what that means. There is a dash as well. Or perhaps "SRR."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I can assist, I think that Judge Fluegge is referring to what appears to the letter K and R at "crisis" before "staff."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There is a handwritten line. Do you know what that means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only thing I see is a semicircle, a line. That's what I see on my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Have you any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have no clue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could next go to 65 ter 14471A.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, this is an excerpt from a book about the Seselj Chetnik movement. We'll be looking at an order that is reprinted from that book or reprinted in the book. And, sir, as you see the document come up, you see that it's dated 20 March 1994. I would direct your attention down to the prominent number 1. It describes an individual, Vidovic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: Can you tell us if you ever seen this document which is now on
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: After describing his efforts elsewhere, towards the end we read: "At the end of February 1992, he went to the Sarajevo-Ilijas ... where he still is today."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Part of the quote --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- was the word "battle-field."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: "Sarajevo-Ilijas battle-field where he is today." Do you know this individual?

utterances.speaker: Can you tell us if you ever seen this document which is now on
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you know him to be a Seselj fighter or one of the Seselji?

utterances.speaker: Can you tell us if you ever seen this document which is now on
utterances.text: He presented himself as a member of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And did he participate as part of the Serb forces for Ilijas starting in February of 1992?

utterances.speaker: Can you tell us if you ever seen this document which is now on
utterances.text: Yes, in TO units. But exclusively under the command of the Territorial Defence, nobody else's, irrespective of party affiliations.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: After the TO did he become part of the brigade under the VRS?

utterances.speaker: Can you tell us if you ever seen this document which is now on
utterances.text: Yes. He was the commander of an intervention platoon of the Army of Republika Srpska in the Ilijas Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 65 ter 14471A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 14471A receives number P6696, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that is only the excerpt [Microphone not activated] That's only the excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I'm sorry. I should have explained it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Just that portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, P6696 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to shift topics a bit and go back to some areas that you touched on earlier today in your testimony. And that has to do with the departure of non-Serbs from Ilijas. You testified that individuals had a right to leave and that there was, I believe, free departure. In order to leave, did Bosniaks need to have your permission?

utterances.speaker: Can you tell us if you ever seen this document which is now on
utterances.text: Not from me. They were supposed to report to the Red Cross in order to be provided with passes, because the police units at check-points had an order to the effect that if they had such passes, they were not supposed to be stopped at those check-points or prevented from crossing them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could look at 65 ter 31131.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, this appears to be an authorisation signed by you allowing certain named Bosniaks to leave Ilijas. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: Can you tell us if you ever seen this document which is now on
utterances.text: I recognise the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. Let's start at the top left-hand -- the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether you recognised the document. Do you recognise the document? No, you said you recognised the signature. Do you recognise the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. May I explain the whole situation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: First, I should clarify. The signature, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: Can you tell us if you ever seen this document which is now on
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And the upper left-hand corner of this letter indicates that it comes from the command of the 1st Sarajevo-Ilijas Brigade, and it appears to be dated 29 June 1992. Sir, next to your -- or above your signature, your title is commander. So can you tell us your position at that time as of the 29th of June 1992?

utterances.speaker: Can you tell us if you ever seen this document which is now on
utterances.text: My position was as the president of the municipality. Those were chaotic times. Somebody typed up the document. I remember this case. The brigade command and the check-points where people were checked at the separations lines could not meet their requests, which is why they came to me to allow them to leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you your position as of the 29th of June 1992. Sir, you have testified now that in order to leave Bosniaks simply needed to have something from the Red Cross. This appears to be a document signed by you as a commander allowing these individuals to leave. I'll put it to you that your testimony, that people had freedom to depart and a right to leave, was not accurate.

utterances.speaker: Can you tell us if you ever seen this document which is now on
utterances.text: No, those were exceptional situations. And as I've already said, the times were chaotic. And sometimes there were discrepancies in the Red Cross and in the brigade command. Then they wanted for my -- asked for my arbitration as to how to proceed, and then I suggested that people should be allowed to move freely wherever they wanted to go. If there was anything in dispute, I mean. And whoever typed up the word "commander" is a mistake. I was not a brigade commander. I may have not paid too much attention when I approved this request. In any case, I was not a commander. I was only the president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a question. Sir, just in response to the answer you've just given, the heading of that letter says: "Command of the 1st Sarajevo-Ilijas Brigade." Didn't you see that when you signed the letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That document was drafted in agreement with the command, because --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I stop you. My question is: Did you not see the words "Command of the 1st Sarajevo-Ilijas Brigade" when you signed this letter? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not of major importance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not decisive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you see the words, yes or no? You have been told so many times to please concentrate on the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Don't talk when I'm talking. Don't talk.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have been told many times to concentrate on the question and answer the question and not give your explanations. Did you see these words before you signed this letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is very possible that I did not. At that moment it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- simply not important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Stop there. Did you also not see the word "commander" above your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, it was of no importance at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
